data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Ok, I've found some clues.<br>
Adding the <code class="notranslate">enable_widevine=1</code> flag actually made it compile the Widevine plugin components. They just weren't added to the <code class="notranslate">Chromium.app</code> package for some reason. The files <code class="notranslate">libwidevinecdm.dylib</code> and <code class="notranslate">widevinecdmadapter.plugin</code> are inside the <code class="notranslate">/out</code> folder. I tested them and they work, enabling playback on that test site as well on Netflix.</p>
<p dir="auto">However, a <code class="notranslate">manifest.json</code> file is also required  for Widevine and, for some reason, it isn't being build. I discovered this by downloading Google Chrome and looking into their <code class="notranslate">.app</code> folder. There, I found the 2 Widevine files plus the <code class="notranslate">manifest.json</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">On OS X, you can get Widevine support on ungoogled-chromium by doing this:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Create a file with the name <code class="notranslate">manifest.json</code> and the following contents:</li>
</ol>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "update_url": "https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx",
  "name": "WidevineCdm",
  "description": "Widevine Content Decryption Module",
  "offline_enabled": false,
  "version": "1.4.8.903",
  "minimum_chrome_version": "47.0.2526.0",
  "x-cdm-module-versions": "4",
  "x-cdm-interface-versions": "8",
  "x-cdm-host-versions": "8",
  "x-cdm-codecs": "vp8,vp9.0,avc1",
  "icons": {
    "16": "imgs/icon-128x128.png",
    "128": "imgs/icon-128x128.png"
  },
  "platforms": [
    {
      "os": "win",
      "arch": "x86",
      "sub_package_path": "_platform_specific/win_x86/"
    },
    {
      "os": "win",
      "arch": "x64",

    },

    },
    {
      "os": "mac",

    }
  ]
}"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">{

<ol start="2" dir="auto">
<li>Get inside your <code class="notranslate">Chromium.app</code> package, and go to <code class="notranslate">Contents/Versions/your_chromium_version/Chromium Framework.framework/</code></li>
<li>Create a <code class="notranslate">Libraries</code> folder there</li>
<li>Inside it, paste the <code class="notranslate">WidevineCdm</code>folder from the <code class="notranslate">/out</code> folder.</li>
<li>Put the <code class="notranslate">manifest.json</code> inside the <code class="notranslate">WidevineCdm</code> folder.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">It should work now. Alternatively, you can just download Chrome and copy the Libraries folder from their package - it also works, even if the Chromium and Chrome versions don't match.<br>
Putting these files inside a <code class="notranslate">Chromium.app</code> package that was built without the <code class="notranslate">enable_widevine=1</code> flag doesn't work.</p>
<p dir="auto">The Windows/Linux builds might be getting similar behavior (<code class="notranslate">widevinecdm.dll</code>/<code class="notranslate">libwidevinecdm.so</code> files left in the out folder without being used). We probably can get Widevine support in a similar way with them.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1
